newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares slide on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares slide on profit-taking.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial shares slid more than four percent on Tuesday, dragged down by profit-taking which brokers said looked set to continue for a few more days before the market stabilised.
The key 57-counter industrial index fell 491.22 points or 4.2 percent to end the day at 11,284.70.
"All the big caps had some big markdowns today. I think it's just some price correction and we might see the index come down a few more points before it stabilises," one broker said.
"People are just taking their profits after the market's run but we might see some buyers coming back soon," another one said.

Among the day's losers, winery Cairns fell 260 cents to 1,400, hotel and supermarket group Meikles slid 250 cents to 2,800 while hotels, supermarkets and beverages conglomerate Delta and tea producer Tanganda each dropped 200 cents to 1,900 and 600 respectively.

Merchant banker NMB shed 75 cents to 3,425, clothing and furniture retailer H and S lost 60 cents to 400, agricultural and rubber products manufacturer Acacia traded 30 cents off at 270 and industrial investor TZI was 25 cents lower at 875.
A couple of counters bucked the trend -- cement producer Circem which rose 25 cents to 725 and finance house Finhold which gained 20 cents to 720.

Minings were firmer with gold producer Rio Tinto -- which earlier said it had closed its Brompton mine on the back of depleted reserves and recent falls in the bullion price -- rising 100 cents to 1,700.
Nickel miner Bindura added 30 cents while Wankie Colliery was the day's sole loser, trading 20 cents down at 800.
The mining index put on 16.48 points to close at 840.65.
